key_insight: DeepRoot combines a verified knowledge graph with multi-agent LLM reasoning to turn historical medical texts into more reliable therapeutic hypotheses than standard LLM or tool-using baselines.
clinical_relevance: This could help surface new drug-repurposing leads from legacy medical knowledge, but it is a discovery aid rather than a basis for clinical decision-making.
method: Extracts entities and relations from historical medical prose into a verified knowledge graph
Uses multiple coordinated LLM agents to reason over the graph and generate treatment hypotheses
Separates grounding from reasoning to improve both factual support and interpretability
evidence_signal: On the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing, DeepRoot recovered 10 of 21 held-out compound-disease pairs at R@20 (47.6%), outperforming a raw-corpus LLM (4.8%) and random (~2.4%), while hallucinating evidence on only 7-10% of claims versus 87% for tool-using LLMs.
watch_item: Results come from a single historical source and held-out benchmark, so broader generalization, graph construction quality, and translation of hypotheses into validated drugs remain uncertain.
paper_title: DeepRoot: A KG-Coordinated Multi-Agent System for Therapeutic Reasoning over Historical Medical Texts
